title: Distinct character degrees of the symmetric group
credit: On the irreducible character degrees of symmetric groups and their multiplicities, arXiv:2410.01726 (2024)
premise_risks: arXiv:2410.01726 (preprint, refereeing status unclear): the numerical data for n <= 129 and the suggested limit near 2.5 are context only; Claim does not depend on them.
plain: Conjugate partitions always give representations of S_n of the same dimension, so at most (p(n)+sc(n))/2 of the p(n) irreducible representations can have distinct dimensions, where sc(n) = o(p(n)) counts self-conjugate partitions; so at most half asymptotically. Decide whether the fraction of distinct dimensions tends to a limit, and whether that limit is positive.
math: Let d(n) = #{f^λ : λ ⊢ n} be the number of distinct irreducible character degrees of S_n and p(n) the number of partitions of n. Prove or disprove: d(n)/p(n) converges to a positive limit L as n → ∞.
review_note: arXiv:2410.01726 supplies multiplicity data only and does not pose this question.
